about: Every check CI runs, one entry each, in the order each shard runs them (PLAN.md 19k).
`checks.yml` runs a shard as `node scripts/checks.mjs --ci <shard>`; `reach.mjs` reads
which shards a PR's diff selects from here; `npm run quick` runs, in parallel, the
checks a diff reaches. A new check is one entry here (and its npm script, if it has
one), never a new step in the workflow. `why` is the step's old comment: what the
check measures and why it is where it is. `always`, on a Measure check, keeps it in
the selection when a PR's diff reaches only some Measure checks (PLAN.md 19k-4): the
cheap ones that hold the rest. `scripts/checks.mjs` holds the rules.

checks.name: The scripts parse
checks.run: for f in scripts/*.mjs server/*.js dc.mjs; do node --check "$f" || exit 1; done
why: Every script parses (PLAN.md 19b). `tsc` reads only a handful of the
harnesses, so a syntax error in one that only a Mac shard runs used to
be found after the Mac queue; this finds it in about three seconds.

checks.name: The manifest of checks
why: This file, the workflow that runs it and the rules that pick a PR's
shards from it (scripts/checks.mjs, PLAN.md 19k): every check's npm
scripts and files exist, checks.yml runs each part and shard from here
and no check beside it, the trace finds every script esbuild finds a
check importing, and each selection rule beside its control.

checks.name: The workflows lint
why: actionlint, a pinned release checked against its published sha256
(scripts/actionlint.mjs, PLAN.md 19k-3), over .github/workflows. CLAUDE.md
asked every session that touched a workflow for it, and none could run it:
nothing in the repository fetched it. A workflow that does not parse, an
expression on a context that is not there or a `needs` that names no job
is a deploy that never starts; here it is a red in four minutes.

checks.name: What a change reaches
why: The list of what cannot reach a Mac shard, held to the paths it was
written for (checks.yml's reach job uses it to skip the Mac).

checks.name: The plate
why: Every preset's dish: that its dyes, injection styles and liquids all
name things that exist. The cheapest check in the repo and the one that
catches a rename that a type cannot.

checks.name: Area cords (the gate and the tables)
why: Areas that listen (PLAN 25h): the area cords' gate, timed, and every
look's area cords on areas it has and fast readings it really has. The
lab half, the cords on the real solver, runs on the Mac (plate shard).

checks.name: The desk
why: That a look change never cuts the plate to black in front of a room.

checks.name: The desk's layouts
why: The desk's layouts (Desk v2): what ships, what is stored, and that a
stored layout from an older build cannot break the desk.

checks.name: The phone link's QR code
why: The Phone · iPad panel's QR code (PLAN 8f), read back module by module:
the format and version words, every Reed-Solomon block, the bytes.

checks.name: The turntable
why: The spinning dish's CPU half: the liquid's lag behind the glass, Auto
Spin's rate and its tempo lock, and the hand on the Spin tool (PLAN §22).

checks.name: The slosh
why: The tilt slosh's physics on the TypeScript reference (PLAN 18a-13a, 13d):
two layers of shallow water that ring at the gap's wave speed, settle on
a held tilt, damp at the drag's rate, break into bores at Stoker's speed,
float an oil lens and ring out from a press, and stay bounded. Four
processes side by side, about five minutes.

checks.name: The panel
why: The two lists that have to agree about what a control is: the settings
panel's own markup, and the registry the desks pin from.

checks.name: Buttons say their state
why: Every button drawn by a state says it, in the lit look (scripts/states.mjs,
PLAN.md 35a): the source read for a className that changes with a state
and no aria-pressed, -selected or -checked beside it, which the browser
half (Switches read on and off) cannot see. A second, no browser.

checks.name: The check-change guard
why: The guard on a check's bars and inputs, against #362's two real cases
and the things it must not fire on (comments, names, prose, printing).

checks.name: A closed PR stops its runs
why: The workflows' own wiring: closed.yml cancels a merged PR's runs by
joining their concurrency groups, which it spells by hand, and the
gallery runs on its label rather than on every push (PLAN.md 19a).
A rename in one file would quietly undo either.

checks.name: The API scripts keep the token out of their errors
why: The scripts that read GitHub's API never print the token: a 502 from
it once printed the owner's whole token through flakes.mjs's error.
Against a local server that answers 502, with the old way as control.

checks.name: The ear
why: The ear: synthetic songs through the real matcher, and the tempo
sources through the real beat clock.

checks.name: Where songs end and begin
why: Where songs end and begin (PLAN.md 14z): eight real songs in
scripts/fixtures/songs, decoded by the ffmpeg installed above, joined
with gaps, gapless and crossfaded, in a quiet room and a noisy one,
through the app's ear into the boundary; every song whole with no
change inside it; and the local matcher naming each crossfade's new
song. About two minutes on the runner's cores.

checks.name: Sound learn
why: Sound learn: controls bound to the music. A synthesised song through
the analyser, the beat clock and the trigger engine frame by frame: a
kick trigger fires once per kick and never on a hat, ahead of the heard
onset once the clock is locked; a mapping moves its setting by its depth
and two add and clamp; the map file round-trips; and with the music
stopped nothing fires.

checks.name: The song's shape
why: The song's shape (PLAN.md §10, step 2): builds, drops and breakdowns
heard live. Synthesised songs whose sections are known to the sample
(four on the floor at 90 to 140 bpm, 20 dB down, a build that keeps
its kick, a rock song with fills): every drop within a bar and none
anywhere else, builds before their drops, breakdowns within four bars,
nothing at all in two minutes of groove, the same at 30 fps, triggers
bound to each fire once per event; then the shelf, decoded by the
ffmpeg installed above, held to at most a drop a minute.

checks.name: Following a song
why: Following a known song played live (PLAN.md 28g): a map made from one
recording, as the app makes it, followed through takes 15% slower and
faster on other instruments, with the bridge left out, the last chorus
twice, the solo twice as long and a jam the song never had: within a
bar of the true place, the tempo within 5%, back within four bars of a
change, and confidence falling in the jam. Arithmetic only, so `logic`.

checks.name: The kicks
why: The kicks (PLAN.md §14d): the show's own band, its score rendered to
samples at 48 and 44.1 kHz and heard through the live ear, with the
plate at 60, 30 and 20 fps and frames late, and the ear reading at
60 Hz under a slower plate: every section's kicks heard by the clock
and by the ear itself, the song's shape counting them, the lock
within the first bars; and the old ear, the smoothed bass crossing
its line, missing the chorus as the Mac did.

checks.name: The breakdown
why: A breakdown is quieter on the plate (PLAN 28d): the band's chorus, its
verse 8 dB down, the chorus, through the ear a render uses. The old
bass press changes more a second in the breakdown (the control, as on
the showreel), the new one at most three quarters as much as in the
groove, the hands fall with the passage, and a song quiet all through
or a volume turned down is learned as the new level. Ten seconds.

checks.name: A click is not a beat
why: A click is not a beat (PLAN.md 14x): the ear in arithmetic, a click a
tick and a thump, in a quiet room and under the band. With no gesture
marked it takes the clicks for kicks (the control); marked, no onset in
a click's moment at 10 to 200 ms of input latency, every kick of the
band outside one still heard, and the beat clock firing the band's
kicks through them. At 48 and 44.1 kHz. About a minute and a half.

checks.name: The one
why: The one (PLAN.md §10, step 3): the beats and which of them is the one,
on eight synthesised songs whose bars are known (four on the floor
and a rock beat, a chord a bar or every two), 20 dB down, at 30 fps,
and after a gap into a new tempo: a real beat named within 70 ms at
the song's tempo, no kick but the one ever called the one, every kick
weighed exactly what its place says; a pulse and three loops with no
bar never placed, on a beat they do hear; fuzzed onset streams never
naming a tempo outside the range nor hanging (a child process with a
deadline); an estimate's median and 99th percentile cost; and the
accent at 0 leaving every kick at exactly 1. About a minute and a half.

checks.name: Pacing
why: Pacing (PLAN.md §10, step 1): a running sequence's stages played as
scenes. At Pacing 0 every built-in sequence hands the plate exactly 1
and 1 and fires nothing; "Light Show Night", measured with the
footage's own yardstick, swells 1.5 to 3.5 a minute and is calm 20 to
40 % of the time; dark endings reach near-black without a step; and a
locate neither piles moments up nor loses them.

checks.name: Slow Evolve
why: Slow Evolve (PLAN.md §10, step 8): one move at a time, each glided 30 to 90 s,
about one a minute; the lean livelier after drops than in breakdowns,
the palette turning only at a drop or a breakdown (or every few
minutes with no music); a level shaken every half second leaning as
the steady song does; and nothing that moves the whole picture moved.

checks.name: The render's clock, ear and file
why: A song render's arithmetic (PLAN.md §6): the show clock is the frame
number while rendering and the browser's own clock live; the song's
track is the same bytes twice and hears the kicks at the same moments
at 30 and 60 fps; the ear the render uses is the live hook's to the
last bit; and both file writers give back every sample, at its time,
through a strict reader, the same bytes twice; and ffprobe, installed
above for the shelf, opens each file with the right streams, every
packet and the right length (with no ffprobe this fails on CI).

checks.name: The ladder's shape
why: The shape of the quality ladder: that every rung is a rung, that a
step down gives something up, and that a rung asking for fewer device
pixels actually gets fewer. That last one was inert for a long while
and nothing looked.

checks.name: The liquids
why: Soap, milk, silicone and glycerine, each measured on the thing it is
for — and first, that an empty plate is left completely alone.

checks.name: Each liquid's own colour
why: Each liquid pours its own colour (syrup amber, glycerine clear, milk
white), and a dye picked for it tints it by Beer and Lambert.

checks.name: The liquids file
why: A liquid someone made: the file reads back as what they meant, a bad
one says why, and "how it meets the others" agrees with the shelf.

checks.name: The popped bubbles
why: A popped bubble closes back into the liquid, round, not into blocks.

checks.name: Bubble and bead physics
why: Bubbles and beads live by physics, not timers (PLAN.md §18i).

checks.name: Blow's range
why: Blow's Amount from a breath that only ripples the colour to a gale (PLAN.md
QA-20): no air taken in below the speed the surface tears at, as much as
ever at the default, more past it, a rate a second; the straw as the breath.

checks.name: The drops
why: Drops, not rings (PLAN.md batch 3): on a plate a current has crowded,
each drop its own colour, pressed flat where it touches, a swallowed
one kept inside and let go, and at 0 the rings' field to the bit.

checks.name: The film table
why: A soap film's own colours (Film Physics): the research's film.py to a level of
8-bit colour, the textbook sequence in the shader's table, and the shader carrying it.

checks.name: The draining soap film
why: A draining vertical soap film seen in reflection (PLAN 32a): 2D Darcy
buoyancy convection, conservative minmod advection, evaporation to Newton
black, and Airy's reflectance at an angle.

checks.name: The dish that boils
why: Heat the performer rides (PLAN 36e): the lamp's hot spot through the dye,
warm water rising by its real density on an upright plate and not at all on
a level one, a nucleation superheat per site, a boil where a hand blocks the
air that holds near 100 °C, and calm within seconds of letting go.

checks.name: A row's fade
why: A Mixer row taken out over bars and brought back (PLAN.md §11 step 4):
whole fades driven at the show timer's 16 ms, no step past the curve's
steepest, the turn-round, the hand, the cut, and the pads wired.

checks.name: The back plate's own look
why: The back plate's own look (PLAN.md §16a): the fold hands plate 1 the
look's solver keys under the live patches and leaves the picture the
front's, the fade is a Go's, Follow lets go, and the pours are wired.

checks.name: The set list file
why: The set list file: a show's running order reads back as it was written.

checks.name: The one Record button
why: The one Record button (PLAN 14ae): what a press does for each choice,
and one Record on the desk, the panel and the phone.

checks.name: The song's score
why: The score (PLAN 28h): each of a song show's cues drawn where the
scheduler fires it, a cue pinned to a section firing on that section
through a stretched live take, and the nudge putting a late map's cue
back on the song's turn without firing a section's cue twice.

checks.name: Settings survive the sanitiser
why: A setting from a menu, the phone or a saved look survives sanitizePatch
(PLAN.md QA-29, 14n): every value every choice setting can take, every
preset intact, malformed patches, gestures and MIDI maps dropped.

checks.name: The privacy page matches the code
why: The privacy page names everything that leaves the machine (PLAN.md
23.13): every host the code reaches, every VITE_ service it is built
with, and no {{OWNER: …}} mark left on it or on the terms.

checks.name: The frame holds still
why: The band moves the liquid, not the frame (Frame Sway, lib/plateRock.ts):
through a song's kicks, every shipped look and show stage slides the
whole picture 0% a frame, against up to 1% with the cover glass free
as #347 shipped it; the app's own frames are held to it in render-app.

checks.name: The looks' sound patches
why: The looks' sound patches read something, and a patch can hear the
hits (PLAN 28f): every shipped patch moves its control (four named a
drum on a source without one and read 0), and each drum's hit reaches
a patch on its frame, at its strength, and is gone between hits.

checks.name: Hold keeps the closeup
why: Hold stays where the closeup is (PLAN.md QA-12): the real closeup
camera on a made-up plate, switched to Hold from Auto and from Follow,
moves the frame on main's Hold and not on this one.

checks.name: The closeup holds still
why: The closeup holds still (PLAN.md 27a-8, QA-30): the real closeup camera
through a song at 6x gives the same centre and zoom as in silence on
every shipped look with Frame Sway at 0, and sways and pumps with it at
full; a kick's press under the drop no longer throws the lead; a drop on
still paint does not shiver.

checks.name: The seed
why: The same seed plays the same show (PLAN.md §6, lib/rng.ts): nothing in
src draws from Math.random outside a short allowlist of ids, and the
beads, bubbles, closeup camera, chemistry, palette and automation run
twice on one seed come out the same, on another seed differently, and
none of them moves another's numbers.

checks.name: The room
why: The room sensor: painted rooms through the real analysis, a closed
feedback loop, and a person who walks in and stops.

checks.name: The sound cords
why: A sound cord's shape (PLAN 30a): tone bursts in and out of a dragged
band, fires counted against the threshold and timed against the attack
and release. Written before the build, so only its controls run until
30a lands (the tape, the counter on today's area-cord gate, and every
saved cord folding as before); the build's PR drops `--controls`.

checks.name: The shapes
why: Four harnesses that were written as gates and then never gated
anything, because nothing here ran them. All four cover arithmetic
with no picture in it, which is the kind most able to be quietly
wrong: a triangle that is really a sawtooth, a timecode reader two
frames behind all night, a fixture lit on the wrong channel, a shape
mapped onto the wrong part of a wall.

checks.name: The closeup's cells
why: The closeup's drawn cells ride the paint and hold still between
frames (lib/detailFlow.ts): frame by frame they move as far as the
dye did, through frame-time noise, dropped frames, 20 to 144 Hz, the
tempo and the lean changing and Speed pulled to nothing; their clock
wraps cleanly; and packing the flow adds no rounding of its own.

checks.name: The report Worker
why: The crash-report Worker, against in-memory R2 and KV (crash-plan.md):
a report is stored with its picture beside it and indexed by the line
it died on; the wrong kind, bad JSON and an oversized body are refused
without quoting them; the digest folds lines that differ only in their
numbers into one group and is closed without the token; and one
address is held to its hourly limit. The endpoint is public, so most
of what it proves is what it will not do.

checks.name: The song-ID Worker
why: The song-ID Worker (scripts/fingerprint-worker.mjs, PLAN.md 14o): every
lookup it passes on is paid for from the owner's account and its
address is in the public bundle, so what is checked is mostly what it
refuses (another site, no Origin, an oversized or unsized body, the
31st an hour from one address or /64, the day's ceiling, no counter
store), each read twice: the status, and that the service was never
called. Node's Request and FormData only, so `logic`.

checks.name: The Mac app's updates
why: The Mac app's updates (scripts/updates.mjs, PLAN.md 13-update): what
desktop/updates.js does with each thing electron-updater says, above
all what it must not do by itself in the middle of a set, and that the
build, the app and the site agree on where a release's .dmg is. Plain
Node with stand-ins for Electron, so `logic`; the real updater against
a feed is `npm run desktop -- --packaged`, in desktop.yml.

checks.name: Cloud sync between two devices
why: Cloud sync for Pro (PLAN.md 23.18, scripts/cloudsync.mjs): two devices,
each with its own storage like a browser and the Mac app, syncing through
the licence Worker's /sync against in-memory KV with real RS256 tokens.
Node only, so `logic`.

checks.name: The shaders compile
why: Every shader compiles, on SwiftShader, in two seconds (PLAN.md 19b).
It runs again on the Mac's show shard, against Metal; here it is found
before the Mac queue rather than after it.

checks.name: Lamp Ground 0 is the plate before the lamp
why: Lamp Ground 0 is the plate as it was before the lamp, byte for byte,
every look (PLAN 18b, 19z): two labs, one built with the lamp's lines
taken out, compared on SwiftShader, which lampzero reads back from the
adapter rather than trusting the flags. Here and not on the Mac
because it compares two compiled programs: Metal on an M4 fused a
multiply-add on the back plate's painted path differently in the two,
and one pixel of Fillmore read 2 levels off (2026-10-11, main at
b2ca7d7), while the CPU rasteriser's arithmetic is the shader's text.
Its own part: `logic` has no Chromium (this step's first run failed
there on the launch, 2026-10-12), and `browser` already runs twelve of
its fifteen minutes. About five minutes; the lamp's physics stay on
the open shard (`lamp`). Since the lab part split in two (below, `lab2`
is lampzero, bubblelook and the four account checks) it shares a runner
with those, about ten minutes, and `lab` keeps the slosh dish, the soap
film and holeline, about twelve.

checks.name: Looks on a lit stage
why: A look keeps its contrast over a projector's black lifted by a stage
wash (PLAN 36a): every look over a floor of 5 and 10% of white added
as light, its dye against the field behind it held with Lit stage on,
and byte for byte the plate without the grade at 0. Written before
the build, so only its controls run until 36a lands (the measure, the
floor's cost with nothing done); the build's PR drops `--controls`.
On SwiftShader for lampzero's reason (b3 compares two compiled
programs, which is the CPU rasteriser's to judge), but in `browser`,
not beside it in `lab`: the lab part already runs 23-24 of its 25
minutes on a slow runner, and this PR's lab part was cancelled at
the limit twice with this check in it (2026-10-27). About a minute
here, three to four in full: the build's PR weighs where it fits.

checks.name: The slosh dish on the GPU
why: The slosh dish's GPU kernels are the reference scheme (PLAN 18a-13a, 13d;
scripts/sloshgpu.mjs): the two-layer dish stepped on the GPU and in
TypeScript through a tilt, a rocked oil lens, a press, a kick's dome and
a bore, held together to a ten-thousandth, cell by cell. `npm run slosh`
holds the TypeScript to the physics; this holds the shader to it. It runs
again on the Mac's plate shard, against Metal.

checks.name: The draining soap film on the GPU (control)
why: The draining soap film's GPU check against its CPU control (PLAN 32c,
scripts/soapgpu.mjs --selftest, scripts/soapgpu-cpu.ts): the CPU reference
in the GPU solver's contract through every scenario and bar of soapgpu.
In Measure's lab part rather than logic because soapgpu.mjs opens the lab
page in Chromium and requests a WebGPU adapter before running the solver,
and checks.yml installs Chromium only on the browser, lab and lab2 parts.

checks.name: No line round a bubble's hole
why: No line round a bubble's hole in one dye (PLAN.md 33a,
scripts/holeline.mjs). The owner saw bubbles drawn with a blocky dark
outline: the edge line between two dyes fired on the depth step at a
hole's rim, sampled on the solver's cell grid. The line now waits for
the dye's colour to change, and this check builds a second lab with
that gate cut out, so the halo it measures away is found again in the
same run, and the line between two real dyes is still drawn. It also
holds PLAN.md 33b: the dye's relief is flat beside a hole (a third lab
with airNear's mask taken off finds the glow again), and a pool's edge
into clear liquid keeps its relief. It reads pictures from the lab, which SwiftShader renders as the shader's text,
so it sits here beside lampzero rather than in the Mac queue.

checks.name: A bubble's middle is the plate
why: A bubble's clear middle is the plate (PLAN.md 33e, scripts/bubblelook.mjs).
The owner saw bubbles as donuts: the projected middle was the dye's
hue at 41-77 % strength, so a dim dye-coloured disc sat inside a black
band. This check builds a second lab with the old line put back, so
the donut it measures away is found again in the same run, on the
dark ground and the lamp ground, at five sizes. Pictures from the lab,
which SwiftShader renders as the shader's text, so it sits beside
holeline in the open shard.

checks.name: Sign-in
why: Sign-in and account management (PLAN.md 23.10, scripts/signin.mjs):
against the Firebase Auth emulator, Google, Apple and magic-link
sign-in, offline returning sessions, sign-out and account deletion.

checks.name: One address
why: One address (PLAN.md 23.16, scripts/onehost.mjs): chromaglass.web.app and
chromaglass.firebaseapp.com forward to chromaglass.art with what they had
saved, written before the app's module runs; Firebase's /__/ pages, an
offline or internet-less cached show and a cast window with an opener
stay; a carried fragment from anywhere else writes nothing. index.html
served at the real names through request routing, under a minute.

checks.name: Linking devices by account
why: Linking devices by account (PLAN.md 23.14, scripts/accountlink.mjs):
two signed-in pages on the same account (a show and a phone) list and
join the show in one tap while keeping the QR code, a third page on
another account sees nothing, and losing the internet keeps local
remote control up.

checks.name: Licensing and tiers
why: Licensing and tiers (PLAN.md 23.2, 23.4, 23.5, 23.6, 23.11,
scripts/tiers.mjs): offline Ed25519 signature verification, 2-machine
limit, Home->Pro upgrade, unlicensed gate, free-tier tiles, 15s/720p
caps + corner mark, and logo mark lock.

checks.name: The dish that boils on the GPU (control)
why: The dish that boils, the GPU check against its CPU control (PLAN 36e-2,
scripts/boilgpu.mjs --selftest, scripts/boilgpu-cpu.ts): the CPU reference
in the GPU solver's contract, its fields stored in float32, through every
dish and bar of boilgpu, so each bar is shown to be one the model meets.
In a Measure lab part because boilgpu.mjs opens the lab page in Chromium
and asks for a WebGPU adapter before it runs the solver; lab2, the lighter
of the two since #517 (10:55 against 14:22). About 80 s in a cloud session.
`npm run boilgpu` itself, on Metal, joins the plate shard with the GPU
build (36e-2): until then it is red by design, as soapgpu was before 32c.

checks.name: The layout
why: The layout, which is CSS and needs no GPU (scripts/layout.mjs): every
control fits, reads, and is not painted over, at every width, and the
mode switch stays put. The same measurements run again inside the show
night on macOS; here they fail in two minutes rather than fifteen, and
before the GPU shards have a chance to hide them behind another step.

checks.name: The cartoons
why: The cartoons that ship (PLAN 14ac): small, silent, recorded in
SOURCES.md, and on a phone page they pour without the pour pausing
every frame (14ab-1), loop, are what the plate and the projector hold,
and stop. No GPU needed: the hand-over is the same without a plate.

checks.name: Preview's copy
why: Preview builds on a copy while the wall keeps its look (PLAN.md 8b,
scripts/draftwall.mjs): which engine each settings change reaches,
what a receiver is sent, Send to wall, Live and the wall closing. Its
line on what the projector window is painted from needs frames, so it
runs again on the Mac's open shard, where it has them.

checks.name: Any camera
why: Any camera, anywhere (scripts/cameras.mjs, PLAN.md 14ad): two stand-in
cameras behind navigator.mediaDevices, nameless until one is allowed.
Both pickers (the motion camera and the film's Webcam) on the desk and
the phone, a camera opened by the id picked, each choice remembered
apart, an unplugged camera taken off and opened again when it is back.
No GPU; the site the steps above built.

checks.name: The phone
why: The phone (scripts/phone.mjs): on an emulated phone, in portrait and
landscape, every tool and sheet in reach at 48 px, the plate keeping
most of the screen, each sheet opening and closing, and Tilt's
arithmetic. The fingers on the plate need WebGPU and are asked on the
open shard below.

checks.name: Saving presets
why: Saving a preset under a name (scripts/saves.mjs, PLAN.md QA-18): on both
desks, a narrow window and the phone, Save asks for a name every time,
saves the settings as they are, lists the preset where that surface
lists presets, and Replace writes over without adding one. No GPU. The
site is already built by the steps above, so the script runs on it
rather than `npm run saves` building it a third time.

checks.name: Switches read on and off
why: Every switch and chosen state reads on and off (scripts/switches.mjs,
PLAN.md QA-30): on the desk, every Settings section, the phone's sheets,
Play and the remote, each control that says it has a state is read in
both, from computed styles. A knob against its track at 3:1, on against
off at ΔE 20 and at 3:1 in light (PLAN.md 35a). Colours, so no GPU; the
site the steps above built.

checks.name: The load
why: The load (scripts/loadtime.mjs, PLAN.md 14v): the built site served
with Brotli over a slowed network, and the page asks for the app's
chunks alongside its entry and for the GPU before the app has
arrived, while the remote and a cast fetch no App chunk; and the
webpage at chromaglass.art (a second build, with a demo sign-in) asks
for its own chunk beside the entry, for the app only once its first
picture is in, and for the GPU only at Play (14v-9). The order is
what is judged, so no GPU is needed and a runner's speed cannot move
it.

checks.name: The intro
why: The intro (scripts/intro.mjs, PLAN.md 14v): drawn by the page before
the app has arrived, taken into the plate's frame on the desk and the

checks.name: The shaders compile
why: Every shader compiles, before anything builds a pipeline from one.

checks.name: The physics
why: The solver's physics on its own: the projection is incompressible
(multigrid against the sweeps), and the magnet draws ferrofluid in
without making, losing or over-packing any.

checks.name: The particles
why: Particles are drawn where their dye is, not at its mirror.

checks.name: The relief
why: The plate's relief (slopes, edges) is worked out where the dye is, not at its mirror.

checks.name: The straw bubble
why: Held still, the Blow grows a bubble with a fingered rim and a ring of satellites.

checks.name: A drop slumps under its own weight
why: A drop of ink on a level plate slumps out along the lower glass as a
viscous gravity current, its front where Huppert's law puts it (PLAN 18m).

checks.name: The press and its lift
why: A press goes down round and lifts into fingers, and a plain spring lift does not.

checks.name: A held press moves only its own neighbourhood
why: A press held in one place (each bubble's) moves the liquid around it,
not the whole plate: the projection's source sums to zero exactly.

checks.name: The press moves the oil
why: A press moves the oil out from under the palm with its colour, onto the
ring the dye lands on, and keeps all of it (PLAN §15d).

checks.name: The wind carries the colour
why: A hand's Blow that is not the straw pushes the colour along and keeps
it, the oil going with its colour; it erased it (PLAN §15c).

checks.name: The spinning dish
why: A spun dish drags its liquid round through the gap, harder where the
gap is tight, flings the heavy dye out and draws the oil in; with
nothing spinning the flow is a still plate's to the bit (PLAN §22).

checks.name: The thin gap
why: Thin Gap (PLAN §18a): a push fades at the drag time 12ν/h², a press
pushes out the volume it displaces and takes it back when the glass
lifts, a tight gap carries what Darcy says, and liquid is conserved
where the gap changes; each against the old solver.

checks.name: The Press comes back on a thin gap
why: The app's own Press on a thin gap: the ring goes out as far as the
displaced volume says with every drop kept, the colour's carry takes
the substeps it needs, and it comes back when the glass lifts.

checks.name: The Finger drags the liquid
why: The Finger on a thin gap as a solid in the liquid: what it touches
moves at the hand's speed, the colour, the ferrofluid and the oil on
its path go with it by the flow alone, nothing is lost, and the
liquid stops with the hand.

checks.name: Areas that listen
why: An area cord works its area and nowhere else (PLAN 25h): a band's cord
on one pool changes the dye, the flow and the heat there 5x what it
changes outside; two areas on two bands each answer their own; and the
rebuilt looks' pours light a place per area where the middle lit one.

checks.name: The wind is air on the film
why: A Blow's wind on a thin gap as air on the film (PLAN 15g): the breath's
stress moves the liquid at τh/2μ, slower in a thick one, stops with
the breath, and carries the colour, the ferrofluid and the oil along
by the flow alone, none lost; the old push alone moved nothing.

checks.name: The forces are forces
why: The plate's forces as forces on a thin gap (PLAN 18a-2): a body force
(Rain Drip's heavy colour, the magnet) moves a liquid as its viscosity
says, Glass Smear is the glass sliding and Updraft a draught's shear,
each against the old reading it replaced.

checks.name: The rides move the plate
why: The rides that barely moved anything (PLAN 27a-c): Plate Rock tips
the plate and the colour slides downhill through the clear liquid as
Darcy says, Beat Squeeze presses the glass across the dish and the
colour goes out and comes back, and Turbulence's dial reaches, each
against what it moved before.
On tools since PLAN 19k: plate ran 19.1 to 20.4 minutes on the PR runs of
2026-10-26 against its 20, and #502's was stopped there with one check left;
this and the rides (or the Ben-Day print), 3.3 minutes, went to tools, at 14.

checks.name: The rock lifts the oil, not the frame
why: Plate Rock lifts the oil (PLAN 27f-5): on a tipped thin gap a lens of
oil rises at Hele-Shaw's speed worked out in SI, its colour does not
hold it down, the rim holds it, and the picture as a whole does not
move with the tilt (the first try slid it 4.2 mm/s every lean).

checks.name: The rhythm sheet is solved
why: Beat Squeeze's sheet solved (PLAN 27f-4): the dent against the theory
of a floating sheet in water, oil and glycerine, exact per mode, its
rim, its release's pace; on the plate the gap is the solve's cell for
cell, its ring past rest, no ratchet, the frame still. In the open
shard: the plate shard is near its timeout.

checks.name: The music pushes the plate
why: The music's own pushes as forces a thin gap keeps (PLAN 27e): Sound
Drive's bass is a hand on the glass that presses as the bass comes in
and lets up as it goes (the burst it replaces moved nothing), and the
energy's swell reads the energy on its own scale. In the open shard:
the plate shard is near its timeout.

checks.name: Bass Boost presses harder
why: Bass Boost is a gain on the bass's hand (PLAN 27g): the old arithmetic
pinned the press and calmed the plate as the slider rose; now the
glass presses deeper and the kicks still press and let go, in the
ear, in the frame loop's source, and on the thin gap in the lab.

checks.name: Each liquid is as thick as it is
why: Each poured liquid as thick as it is (PLAN 18d): on a thin gap a pool
of glycerine falls under Rain Drip at Darcy's 2λ/(1+λ) of a pool of
colour, syrup in a thick look runs ahead of it, a liquid as thin as
the plate's moves as colour alone, and the poured liquid is carried
with its colour and kept: nothing fades it (PLAN 18d-2).

checks.name: The liquids on the GPU plate
why: Soap, glycerine, milk and silicone on the GPU solver's own liquid fields
(PLAN 15e, scripts/liquidsgpu.mjs): the stand-in's four scenes from
`npm run liquids` laid on the thin gap the looks use, each held to the
stand-in's bar and to its size within a factor of two, with a fold of
the deltas every step and on a still plate, and soap's and silicone's
dye asked whether it was moved or erased. Lines owed to PLAN 15e-1 to
15e-5 print and do not fail until they pass. Here on Metal, about a
minute: on the Linux lab part it took 4 min 26 s, and that part ran
24 of its 25 minutes before signin without it (#513's first run).

checks.name: The seed on the GPU, and in the app
why: And the GPU half of the same seed: seeded dye and bubbles through the
solver and the plate shader twice, the same bytes; another seed, not.
Then the built app: ?seed= reaches it, and it says which seed it is on.

checks.name: The microscope
why: The closeup pushes in like a microscope: the cells come through as they resolve.

checks.name: The drop lens
why: An oil drop as a projector throws it (upright, dark past its aperture's core) and as the
closeup's camera sees it (small ones turn the plate over, big ones flat); no highlight.

checks.name: The air lens
why: An air bubble as a projector throws it: a small one a dark disc round a pin-point, a big
one a clear window edged in a band from half the gap; the closeup keeps the camera's bubble.

checks.name: The film, photographed
why: Film Physics on the plate: nothing but the film changes; the projector's bubbles take the
faint tint the light through a film is, the closeup's the soap's own reflected gold.

checks.name: The ferrofluid's edge
why: The ferrofluid is drawn with an edge: a line at any zoom, black all
through, a thin film still visible, the glint fixed as the plate turns.

checks.name: The ferrofluid maze's detail
why: Maze Detail grows finer ferrofluid fingers than the default maze gets
in twice the time, keeps all of it, and the grid floor holds.

checks.name: The slosh dish on Metal
why: The slosh dish's kernels against the TypeScript reference, on Metal
(the same check runs on SwiftShader in Measure's lab part).

checks.name: The draining soap film on Metal
why: The draining soap film's GPU solver (src/gpu/soapFilm.ts,
src/gpu/wgsl/soapFilm.ts) against the CPU reference (src/lib/soapFilm.ts),
on Metal (PLAN 32c, scripts/soapgpu.mjs): first-step face flows within 2%
and thickness change within 5%, 1 s thickness at dt 0.05, 1/60 s and
zeta 0.25 with dt 0.2 s (4 CFL sub-steps) within 5%, C1-C4 and C6,
ruptured hole unrefilled and black spreading within 15%, every step
submitting GPU work and every read mapping a buffer, and the CPU
reference absent from the solver's bundle.

checks.name: The magnet's field
why: The magnet is a disc (PLAN 9v): the shader's field against Biot–Savart,
flatter over its face than the dipole was, a bigger one stronger at the
glass and reaching further, the default's spikes where they were.

checks.name: The ferrofluid's spikes
why: The magnet held close stands the ferrofluid up: the pool parts into
lit domes and its outline stops being a blob's; a look's own far
magnet leaves it whole; a second finger raises domes of its own.

checks.name: The ferrofluid's standing domes
why: The ferrofluid stands up as a layer keeping its volume: flat under the
onset, domes a capillary wavelength apart past it, gaps opening wider
the stronger the field, the domes sinking back down, none lost. In the
open shard: the plate shard is near its timeout (11m58s of 15).

checks.name: The ferrofluid's fingers
why: Past the spikes, the held magnet pulls a big pool's edge out in black
fingers, on Classic and on Magnet Garden; with no magnet or the look's
own far one the edge stays put.

checks.name: The hands move the ferrofluid
why: The Finger and Blow carry the ferrofluid, as they carry the dye; the
tools' push alone (all they did before) leaves it where it was. The
Finger's half is its carry with Thin Gap off; on a thin gap (every
look) the Finger is a solid and `npm run fingerflow` checks it.

checks.name: Colour between the ferrofluid's domes
why: Where the held magnet parts a pool into domes, the water between them
keeps its dye and the plate draws it bright; the maze's flow makes or
loses none of the plate's dye. In the open shard: the plate shard is
near its timeout.

checks.name: The Press on the ferrofluid
why: Thin Gap: a pressed pool of ferrofluid stays full and spreads by the
volume the glass displaced, comes back on the lift, and a front where
the thinner liquid pushes the thicker fingers (PLAN 15d).
In the open shard: the plate shard is near its timeout.

checks.name: The ferrofluid drop in the closeup
why: The closeup's ferrofluid drop (PLAN 29a): its surface the sessile
balance's for its contact angle and size, leaned toward a magnet with
its volume kept, lit from the key's side, coloured by the dye over it;
the plate at 1x the same to the byte. In the open shard, beside the Press.

checks.name: The ferrofluid drop at rest on the thin gap
why: The closeup's ferrofluid drop at rest on the thin gap (PLAN 29c):
degenerate mobility in phaseCHVolume holds its half-full core and
halo against Ostwald ripening into the clear oil, conserves Σc·h, and
does not move without a field, and sheds its half-full cells more
slowly in a second window (steps 200 to 380).

checks.name: The magnet's pull, derived
why: The magnet's pull in tesla, metres and seconds (PLAN 29c-2): the
shader's field against Biot–Savart, the shader's ∇ψ against the
linear Kelvin law (a units check on ψ, the gain cancels there), the
gain against EFH1's, and a drop at the two-phase Darcy speed with the
rim's (ν_clear/ν_ff)^(1−φ) factor applied, under the per-step guard.
On the fifth shard, the lightest (19w), since the open one ran 17.8
minutes of its 20 before the split.

checks.name: The dragged ferrofluid drop holds together
why: The dragged drop while it is dragged (PLAN 29c-8's neighbour): the
ferrofluid carried along itself (phaseMomentum) and what the moving
edge's limiter withheld paid back (phaseCompress), each held on its own
over steps 60 to 180 of `ferrodrag`'s scene (to 120 until 29c-8 kept the
trailing rim to the end of the drag; 29c-10). `ferrodrag` read at three
seconds, red with both passes and without them, so it could not tell. The script
runs the scene three times (as given, phaseMomentum off, phaseCompress
off) and requires each pass to be worth a margin, so the control is in
the run and not done by hand once. On the fifth shard with
`magnetgain`: three scenes of 200 steps.

checks.name: The dragged ferrofluid drop follows the magnet
why: The closeup's ferrofluid drop dragged 0.3 of the plate in three
seconds (PLAN 29c, 29c-8): it follows the magnet within two radii and
keeps its half-full body within 15%, which the two-phase carry of its
trailing rim (phaseVelocity) made true on Metal, 3/3 (out of CI as
known red until then). With no magnet the drop does not move. Its
Thin-Gap-off lines run by hand (`-- --thinoff`, PLAN 29c-11): on Metal
they read the same with the review's fix and without it. On the show
shard, the lightest on #495's run (14.2 minutes of 20); 39 s there.

checks.name: The ferrofluid pushes the dye
why: Pushes Dye: where the ferrofluid grows the colour leaves and packs
along its edge, conserved, and at 0 nothing changes.

checks.name: Oil and water as bodies
why: Oil Bodies: amber oil on teal water stays two colours while the drops
round, merge and turn; poured dye lands in the liquid under it, a
hand drags the oil, nothing is made or lost, and at 0 nothing runs.
Twelve seconds on Metal (#179's run, 17/17), where software WebGPU
takes some twenty minutes; the plate shard ran 8:45 with it in, well
inside its fifteen.

checks.name: No grating over the dye
why: No grating over the dye: the grid's one-cell checkerboard goes in a
second, in every look, and edges, blobs and fine diagonals stay.

checks.name: Dye dispersion along the flow
why: Dye spreads along the flow via shear dispersion (PLAN 18h): streaks
along flow lines while holding sharp cross-stream edges, conserved exactly.

checks.name: The lamp through the dye
why: Lamp Ground (PLAN 18b): on the lamp a clear pool throws the whole lamp,
twice the dye lets through the square, a gel and the back plate filter
through the dye. In the open shard: the plate shard is near its timeout.
"Every look at 0 is the plate as it was before the lamp, byte for byte"
is Measure's (lampzero): it compares two compiled programs, which a
GPU's compiler rounds differently (one pixel of Fillmore on an M4).

checks.name: The heat
why: Heat from the lamp (PLAN 18f): dark dye absorbs heat via Beer–Lambert,
warm liquid rises on an upright plate, viscosity falls ~2%/K, oil floats,
and Newton cooling decays per-second with a tens-of-seconds time constant.

checks.name: Enough colours, and the hues between them
why: More colours (PLAN 18l): most looks carry five dyes and five are on the
plate; a dye is paler thin than deep and a deep yellow turns orange; two
neighbouring dyes meeting walk between their hues; the grade keeps hue.

checks.name: The rim holds the oil that touches it
why: The open rim holds a body of oil that touches it (PLAN 18g-6): held at
the water's pressure in the oil too, the rim drained a lens against it
to 9.6% in six seconds by its own surface tension; held at the oil's
Laplace pressure it keeps it, the middle of the dish is untouched, and
a pour still pushes oil out over the rim. In the fifth shard: the
plate shard is near its timeout.

checks.name: Drops of oil crowd without merging
why: Film Hold (PLAN 28k): the Splodascope's crowd of oil drops stays a
crowd, where the same plate without the hold merges it into a few
bodies; no oil made or lost, and a lone drop untouched. Two 192²
plates of six seconds and two small ones; in the fifth shard, beside
the rim's oil.

checks.name: A pour pushes the liquid out over the rim
why: A pour is liquid (PLAN 18c, 18d-2): water poured at the middle pushes a
ring of colour out by its volume, glycerine poured is all accounted
for, and a dish of glycerine flushed with a quarter of its volume of
water keeps three quarters of it. In the open shard: the plate shard
is near its timeout.

checks.name: A clear film that tears
why: A clear film that tears (PLAN 20b): the film's volume kept, a thick film
whole and a thin dusty one torn into holes of every size by the physics
alone, a drop of solvent opening a growing hole, white over the colour
on the lamp, and the picture unchanged with the film off. In the open
shard, beside the lamp it is drawn on.

checks.name: Clock Glass keeps its colours apart
why: Clock Glass (PLAN 4a-clock): its dish holds several colours apart, in
bodies of oil that keep the colour laid in them, where the old lay was
one blended disc. Two 192² plates of 300 steps; in the open shard, as
the plate shard is near its timeout.

checks.name: The Ben-Day print
why: Ben-Day Dots, the Roy look's print: a pale wash is even dots fixed to
the screen, a pool one flat ink outlined in black, and only Roy prints.
On tools since PLAN 19k: plate ran 19.1 to 20.4 minutes on the PR runs of
2026-10-26 against its 20, and #502's was stopped there with one check left;
this and the rides (or the Ben-Day print), 3.3 minutes, went to tools, at 14.

checks.name: Roy opens as a panel
why: Roy opens as a panel: the app's own seed for the look, printed by the
lab, is paper and three inks with fields of dots, not a black stain.
In the open shard: the plate shard is near its timeout.

checks.name: The mixer's order and grades
why: The mixer: each source moved lands only where that source is (the
film under the back plate, the logo under the film), the LED ring
passes the front plate from lamp to beam, every grade does what its
name says, and every one of the 31 controls changes the picture; the
gel wheel and the lumia in the lamp, over the lens and among the rest.
On the fifth shard since PLAN.md 19w (on show before that, to even it
with plate, 19h); it is the lab, so any shard will do.

checks.name: Beams add, and the seam goes
why: Beams: two projectors of different sources add where they cross, two
carrying one picture sum to it across their overlap with no seam
(the projector's pass on pictures made to order, to the pixel).

checks.name: The ferrofluid through the whole plate
why: Ferro Paint pours its ferrofluid over the whole plate, so after it has
played the black is worked through nearly every part of the colour;
every other look pours exactly what it did.

checks.name: The liquids carried onto a new grid
why: A new grid (the quality governor's move) keeps the plate's liquids
that live only on the GPU: the ferrofluid and the mix in the same
amounts and shape, the reactions value for value (PLAN 9w). In the
open shard: the plate shard is near its timeout.

checks.name: The wall's test pattern
why: The wall's test pattern and Identify (PLAN.md 8e), drawn in the
projector's own pass: off is the plain pass byte for byte, on it is a
grid, cross, circle, border and numbered corners that follow the pin,
the flip and the mask. In the open shard: the plate shard is near its
timeout.

checks.name: Preview's copy, with frames
why: Preview's copy again (see Measure's), here with frames: the projector
window is painted from the wall's canvas and never the copy's.

checks.name: A show night
why: And the show night itself, on the WebGPU stage. It runs here rather
than beside the other one because it needs a GPU: a Linux runner's
software WebGPU can compute but cannot present a canvas (the P0
spike). These runners have Metal, so it also runs at the real device
pixel ratio and on the GPU solver, which the ubuntu job cannot.
A show night on what a visitor actually gets, at the real device pixel
ratio and on the GPU solver — neither of which the ubuntu job can do.

checks.name: The rhythm plate presses on the kick
why: Beat Squeeze presses the lead plate on a kick and lets it go again,
and at 0 presses nothing: counted in the app with the band playing,
on Fillmore East. Until #185 found it, a kick's press landed a
fraction of a cell off the grid and laid nothing, and no check
counted.

checks.name: A song rendered in the app
why: Render this song in the app itself (PLAN.md §6): a synthetic song
rendered ten ways through the visualizer's own frame loop, frame by
frame on the film's clock. The same seed draws the same frames hash
for hash; another seed, a silent song and Evolve each draw others;
a GPU taken away mid-render fails that render and says why; and after
every run the app is given back as it was. It runs here and not on
ubuntu because it needs the app's frames read back, which software
WebGPU does not do. The build above is the one it serves, so this
calls the script and not `npm run render-app` (which builds first).

checks.name: The post chain
why: The post chain in the app: the chain with nothing in it draws the
plate's own picture, the ring keeps what it was given, and the
effects' randomness is the same twice.

checks.name: The show opens without stopping
why: The show opens without stopping (scripts/startup.mjs): what the look
opens with is built before it opens and the rest behind it, none is
built on a frame, no two frames are more than two seconds apart but
for the time Chromium holds the page's whole thread while it starts
its GPU (no frame, timer or long task of the page's, not begun where
a promise it awaits settled, in the first three seconds; held to
4.5 s), and the plate
moves for good no later than it did the old way. On a shard
of its own, because it empties the Mac's shader cache, and one after
another check would find it warm; depth, first on the tools shard,
is how the nine-second freeze was found and still sees it cold.

checks.name: The grain inside the dye, not at its edge
why: The pigment's grain inside the dye, not at its edge: in every look the
grain moves almost no pixel of a dye edge by a fleck's worth (it made
the edges a dithered fringe, "very digital"), and the bodies keep it.
In the open shard (the plate shard is near its timeout), and after the
opening's check, so a timing check never follows four minutes of
renders: with this one before it, startup's first frame waited 2.27 s
on two of the PR's runs, against 1.65-2.00 s on other PRs' runs.

checks.name: The closeup is the liquid, not cells
why: The closeup is the liquid seen closer, not a field of cells (PLAN 33g):
the defaults carry no cell or lacing texture at 4x and 6x, the old
defaults (the control) carry plenty, and the relief is a smooth swell
and sheen that keeps the dye's chroma. The lab only; it runs on the
runner's own adapter (Metal on a Mac), so its time is the Mac's to
measure (npm run macqueue after the first PR run), and the step
carries a timeout of its own so a stuck lab cannot take the shard.

checks.name: The Turing pattern and its print
why: The Turing pattern (PLAN 26): one stripe width on every rung, carried
with the colour and healed after a stir, grown only where it is fed,
and Turing Print black on white where the reaction is, not piling up.
The lab only; five or six minutes on SwiftShader, so on a Mac rather
than in Measure, and on the fifth shard (PLAN.md 19w; it went to show
first, which had the most room then, 13.2 against open's 16.8 on #331's run).

checks.name: The ear behind the wall
why: The show keeps hearing while its window is hidden behind the wall's
(scripts/ears.mjs, PLAN.md §14a): its own frames withheld, a second
window asking for frames as the projector window does, and the level
the plate reads has to keep moving. After startup, on the shard that
finishes first, because it only needs a plate that draws, not a cold one.
Run directly, as render-app is, on the build step's own output.

checks.name: The sound's renders, with a plate
why: The plate hears a new reading nearly every frame while the App renders
ten times a second (scripts/renders.mjs, PLAN.md §14f): the line the
Measure job skips, because there no plate draws. About forty seconds.

checks.name: Audio Impact 0 drops no bubbles
why: Audio Impact 0 holds the music's bubbles back too (scripts/kickbubbles.mjs,
PLAN.md 0-bandbubbles): a fresh browser's first click starts the band,
and its kicks used to drop air near the middle whatever the dial said.
On the laptop and the phone at 0, and at the default, where they still
must (listened to for a minute there, for enough chances). About three minutes.

checks.name: A flicked plate's liquid trails the glass
why: A flicked plate's liquid trails the glass (scripts/flick.mjs, PLAN.md
22h): the look's own turning goes through the liquid's drag time like
the Spin tool's, the picture turns with the liquid, and the flick no
longer stirs the current with a term of its own. It reads the plate's
refs, not its frames, but the frame loop only steps on a GPU that
draws. About twenty-five seconds, on the fifth shard (PLAN.md 19w).

checks.name: Depth reaches the flow
why: The plate's own depth, which until F reached nothing (bubbles-plan.md
F): a domed plate's tight rim has to run slower than its deep centre,
a flat plate has to be untouched however high the dial goes, and a
press has to keep its dent while the glasses change shape under it.
The margins are wide — the rim/centre ratio moves 1.13 to 0.08 where
the gate asks for 10% — because what it guards is a sign and a place,
not a tuning.

checks.name: The magnet moves the ferrofluid
why: The Magnet in the hand (reported: "magnet tool isn't really
working", then "a giant black hole as soon as you pick it"): picked
it changes nothing on the plate, the first touch brings a pool under
the hand as big as Magnet Size, a drag carries that pool with it,
Size reaches the solver, and a new grid (the governor stepping down)
lays nothing but that pool, never the look's ring.

checks.name: The band leaves the ferrofluid where it was poured
why: The ferrofluid poured round Classic's middle, watched with the band
playing and its bubbles on the plate (PLAN.md, found by #238): on the
thin gap it gathers no more than in silence; the old plate, whose
bubbles still press the glass, is shown to drift, so the instrument
sees what it was built for. About a minute and a half.

checks.name: Every tool does what it says
why: Every other tool in the hand (asked for: "check all of the tools to
make sure they work in expected ways"): each does what it says and
nothing else, and hovering does nothing (scripts/tools.mjs).

checks.name: Every tool lays the bottle
why: And the liquid in the bottle, from every tool that lays one: Pour,
Spray, Splat and Streak laid only its colour, so a Ferrofluid Pour
was black dye the Magnet could not move (scripts/bottles.mjs).

checks.name: Draw shows the wall and lands under the finger
why: And from the remote's Draw (scripts/drawwall.mjs --app, PLAN.md
8-draw-a): the laptop's own frames reach the pad, the plate's colour,
and a drop near the wall's corner lands under the finger, where the
plate's point (the old pad) does not. About a minute.

checks.name: The phone's fingers
why: And on a phone, several at once: two fingers are two hands, each
where it is, lifting one leaves the other, two fingers holding Drop
lay dye under both, and on the closeup two fingers pinch the zoom.
On the show shard: about four and a half minutes. It left the tools
shard on 2026-10-03 (a median 13.2 and at most 15.6 against its then
15-minute timeout, PLAN.md 19h) for open, where open finished in 7.8.
Open has gathered eight checks since and on 2026-10-04 ran 17.4 to
18.7 minutes green against its 20, with one run killed by the
timeout inside this step (#280); show ran 8.9 to 10.7. Here open is
about 14 and show about 15 (PLAN.md 19r). Nothing on show needs a
cold shader cache, so the fingers warming it costs no check.

checks.name: A drop lands only where it is dropped
why: A drop lands where it is dropped: on the Design desk, on either layer,
the cell under the hand changes and its mirror image across the middle
does not (reported: an echo of the gesture "in the mirrored section").

checks.name: The ferrofluid's physics
why: And the physics under it: the ferrofluid gathers where the magnet is
(not at its mirror), held close pulls harder than held away, and the
magnet neither makes nor loses liquid.

checks.name: A performance starts and stops by hand
why: Performances start and stop by hand (reported: "the performance auto
detect doesn't work well"): T starts one, nothing painted keeps
nothing, and what is painted is kept, on its own clock with no song.

checks.name: The black box
why: The black box records (crash-plan.md): errors land with a snapshot,
a device loss and its recovery are logged, frames that stop become a
fatal and light the button, a report from a destroyed device still
returns with no screenshot, and the log survives the reload.

checks.name: The wall
why: And the projector's geometry, on a GPU: which pixels are black, and
how many times a second the whole screen is allowed to change.
